matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Before moving any stick, compute the integer values of both sides of the equation and determine the numeric discrepancy that must be resolved.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a matchstick puzzle, before any stick moves.
matchstick.example: Skipping the initial numeric check and moving a stick arbitrarily, resulting in an equation that still doesn't balance.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Systematically enumerate every way a single matchstick can be moved, considering all possible source characters and target positions.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, generate the full set of candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Only considering a few possible moves (e.g., moving a stick from the plus sign) and missing the correct X→V transformation.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, calculate how the move changes the numeric values of the affected numerals and operators, and compare the net change to the required discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating each candidate transformation to see if it can resolve the numeric gap.
matchstick.example: Choosing a move that changes the left side by +3 when the required adjustment is -5, leading to a mismatched total.

matchstick.title: Consider intra‑character repositioning
matchstick.principle: Allow a stick to be moved within the same character, changing its orientation or position to transform the character into another valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a character consists of multiple sticks (e.g., X, V) and a transformation could be achieved by moving a stick within the same character.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from an X to another character, leaving the X with a single diagonal (invalid) instead of repositioning it within the X.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via equals
matchstick.principle: Treat the '=' sign as two horizontal sticks; moving one of its sticks can turn it into a '-' sign, and adding a stick can turn a '-' into '='.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the discrepancy suggests that the equality sign should become a subtraction or addition sign.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to create a '-' but forgetting to add it elsewhere, leaving the equation without a proper equality sign.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick converts it to '-', and adding a vertical stick to '-' creates '+'.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If changing a plus to a minus (or vice versa) could adjust the total by the needed amount.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from '+' and not adding it to any operator, resulting in a missing vertical component.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from one character to another, ensure both the source and target remain valid Roman numerals or operators after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During enumeration of candidate moves that involve different characters.
matchstick.example: Transferring a diagonal from X to a V, causing the source X to become invalid.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved directly from one operator to another, simultaneously changing both operators (e.g., '+' to '-' and '=' to '+').
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single stick move could adjust two operators to meet the required numeric change.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from '+' to '=', turning '+' into '-' and '=' into an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Source character must stay valid after stick removal
matchstick.principle: Before moving a stick, ensure that the source character can lose that stick and still represent a valid Roman numeral or operator (or disappear if it's a single‑stick numeral).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before committing to a stick removal, verify that the source character remains a valid numeral or operator after losing the stick.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X, leaving a single diagonal which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: X↔V intra‑character transformation
matchstick.principle: When an X (two crossing diagonals) or V (two angled sticks) appears, consider moving one diagonal stick within the same character to convert X↔V, which changes its value by ±5; ensure the resulting shape matches a valid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the numeric discrepancy is 5 (or a multiple thereof) and the equation contains an X or V, try converting X↔V by repositioning a diagonal within the same character before exploring inter‑character moves.
matchstick.example: Attempting to change X to V by moving a diagonal to another character, leaving the source X invalid, instead of repositioning the diagonal inside the X.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick without checking that the remaining parts still form a valid symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each candidate move, verify that both the source and target characters correspond to a valid Roman numeral or operator (or disappear if a single‑stick numeral).

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on making a syntactically valid equation but does not recompute the numeric values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After applying a stick move, recompute the integer values of both sides and confirm equality before output.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model truncates the response or forgets to include some characters while moving a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the final answer contains the full equation with all original characters (except possibly a single‑stick numeral that disappears) and exactly one stick moved.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats operator changes as purely syntactic, overlooking their arithmetic effect.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When modifying an operator, recalculate the expression's value to see how the sign change affects the total.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model either forgets the requirement to move a stick or mistakenly outputs the original equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Explicitly track that one stick is relocated: after deciding on a move, ensure the output differs from the input by exactly one stick relocation.
